h: History Hiding Just Behind the Lights
p: It's easy to think of the Golden Mile as nothing but neon and doughnuts, but just a few streets back from Marine Parade lies one of England's most fascinating historic towns. Great Yarmouth grew rich on the herring trade, and its medieval past is still visible if you know where to look. Large stretches of the town walls survive, among the most complete medieval town walls in England, and you can trace them on a walk through the old town.

The town is also known for its Rows, a network of incredibly narrow lanes that once linked the quayside with the market. Many were lost to wartime bombing, but some remain, and the Row Houses run by English Heritage give a glimpse of how people lived in them. The Time and Tide Museum, housed in a former herring curing works, tells the story of the town's fishing past, and it's a brilliant rainy-day option.

Back on the seafront, the Golden Mile has plenty to keep kids entertained. Family arcades are a big part of the strip, with tuppenny falls, grabbers and racing games, while some venues along here are adult gaming centres, which are 18+ only. The Hippodrome Circus, a purpose-built circus building dating from 1903, is just back from the front and still puts on spectacular shows today.

Walk from Britannia Pier south past Sea Life, the gardens and the Marina Centre towards Wellington Pier and you'll get a real feel for the resort. Keep going and you reach the Pleasure Beach, with its historic wooden Scenic Railway coaster, and further south still, the towering Nelson's Monument, which was put up in Nelson's honour decades before the more famous column in London.
